content:
For years, collectors have been avid fans of Jobs memorabilia, and one new lot seems poised to generate significant attention. It's an eighth-grade science fair project, complete with two demonstration circuits — and a warning note written by Jobs to his teacher.

The project has since been kept at the Jobs family property in Los Altos, but it has now become one of over 200 lots in an Apple 50th anniversary auction…

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and RR Auctions held a two-part auction to mark the occasion, called "Jobs and the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction." In the first part, the very first check issued by the company fetched as much as $2.4 million.

The second part includes that science fair project.

The warning note likely reflects the risk of the circuits burning out if left running too long. As of writing, online bids were under $3,000, but we can expect that figure to change.

Also up for auction is a working early Apple 1 computer.

And a development prototype of the original iPod.
